name: Applied Digital
legalName: Applied Digital Corporation (formerly Applied Blockchain, Inc.)
founded: 2021 (pivoted from Bitcoin hosting to AI-factory campuses; fiscal year ends May 31)
employees: Total not disclosed; 200+ per major campus
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Applied Digital holds the largest disclosed base-term lease backlog in the miner-pivot cohort — 1.4 GW of contracted critical IT across five 'AI Factory' campuses, ~$36B over 15-year take-or-pay base terms (~$86B if renewals exercise) — split between CoreWeave (400 MW, ~$11B, Polaris Forge 1 in Ellendale, ND) and a single unnamed 'high investment-grade US hyperscaler' that signed 810 MW / ~$20B across three campuses in FY2026 alone and now represents ~69% of the backlog. The identity of that hyperscaler has never been disclosed and no outlet has confirmed it. FY2026 (ended May 31): revenue $611.3M (+167%), adjusted EBITDA $107.2M, net loss $249.2M; fiscal Q1 2027 (to Aug 31, reported Oct 7): revenue $341.9M, debt $6.4B vs $3.7B cash, live capacity 250 MW at Polaris Forge 1 — with sell-side models so far behind the tenant-fit-out revenue that quarterly beats ran 46–148% above consensus. BACKGROUND: Dallas-based; founded 2021 out of Applied Blockchain; CEO Wes Cummins (ex-B. Riley & Co. president). The funding stack is the story's second half: $6.1B of project notes (9.25%/6.75%/7.00%), a $5B Macquarie perpetual preferred at 12.75% PIK with a 1.80x MOIC floor and 15% of the HPC equity, and debt that went $911M → ~$5.0B in one fiscal year. The GPU-cloud segment was spun out as ChronoScale (NASDAQ: CHRN, ~96% retained) in May 2026; 286 MW of legacy bitcoin hosting is retained. NVIDIA quietly exited its entire ~$177M equity stake in its Q4 2025 13F.
ecosystemRole: We assess Applied Digital as the purest AI-factory landlord in this ecosystem — no GPU cloud (post-ChronoScale), no self-mining conversion story, just build-own-operate campuses on cheap northern-plains power leased for 15 years. For power-chain vendors it is a live, standardized procurement machine: the 'AI Factory franchise model' locks electrical and cooling partners into long-term supplier agreements, builds modular/prefab at PUE 1.18 with waterless direct-to-chip cooling (WUE ~0, 220+ days/year free cooling in North Dakota), and is marketing another 1.7 GW beyond the contracted 1.4 GW — plus a ~10% stake in Base Electron's planned 1.2 GW of gas generation and a $15M bet on Corintis microfluidic cold plates. Basis: company releases and trade coverage; derived lease economics run ~$1.65–1.83M per MW-year against ~$10M+/MW build costs.

productsAndServices.name: AI Factory campuses (HPC hosting — the core business)
productsAndServices.description: Build-own-operate campuses leased under ~15-year take-or-pay contracts: Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale, ND — 400 MW to CoreWeave, ~$11B; 175 MW live as of July 2026), Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND — 200 MW to an investment-grade hyperscaler, ~$5B, tenant ROFR on 800 MW more), Polaris Forge 3 (ND — 300 MW, ~$7.5B), Delta Forge 1 (Boyce, LA — 300 MW, ~$7.5B), and Delta Forge 2 (southern state — 210 MW, ~$5.2B) — the last three all with one unnamed 'high investment-grade' hyperscaler. The 'AI Factory franchise model' replicates a standardized design/construction/operations playbook campus to campus.
highlights: 1.4 GW contracted critical IT; ~$36B base-term revenue, ~$86B with renewals; ~2.15 GW gross grid-connected power
Q4 FY2026 net operating income at a 91% margin; management targets $1B annual NOI within five years, then $2B
Delivery record: first 100 MW energized on schedule Q4 2025; second building (+75 MW) July 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Largest disclosed base-term backlog among the AI-DC landlords (vs Core Scientific ~$10.2B pre-AMD, TeraWulf $12.8B at YE25, IREN's $9.7B Microsoft deal); derived lease rates ~$1.65M (hyperscaler) to $1.83M (CoreWeave) per MW-year.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 15-year take-or-pay leases; project-level 144A notes and the Macquarie preferred finance construction against them.
targetSegments: One unnamed US high-IG hyperscaler (three campuses)
Actively marketing 1.7 GW more across multiple states
productsAndServices.roadmap: PF2 full 200 MW by 2027; Delta Forge 1 mid-2027; Polaris Forge 3 Aug 2027; Delta Forge 2 Q1 2028; PF1 fourth building (ELN-04, 150 MW) financed June 2026.

highlights: Steady cash contributor — not a conversion story like the miner-pivots; no divestiture announced
productsAndServices.positioning: A financing bridge, not the future: cash yield funds corporate overhead while AI Factory campuses absorb the balance sheet.
productsAndServices.roadmap: No stated conversion or sale plans in company materials.

productsAndServices.name: ChronoScale (spun-out GPU cloud, ~96% retained)
productsAndServices.description: The former Cloud Services segment — among the first to deploy NVIDIA H100s at scale in 2023, ~$75M TTM revenue — was separated in May 2026 via combination with EKSO Bionics and trades as ChronoScale Corporation (NASDAQ: CHRN); Applied Digital retained ~96–97%.
highlights: CEO framing: Applied Digital keeps 'long-duration contracts and predictable infrastructure returns'; ChronoScale takes the shorter-cycle cloud risk profile
productsAndServices.positioning: The separation cleaned the landlord thesis — a public-market comp for what the pure-play lease book is worth without cloud volatility.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Separate public entity; consolidated for now given the retained stake.
targetSegments: Enterprise and AI-native GPU compute customers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Watch for deconsolidation or sell-down of the retained stake.

productsAndServices.name: Power & cooling adjacencies
productsAndServices.description: A ~10% equity stake in Base Electron Corp. (1.2 GW of planned natural-gas generation), and a $15M investment leading Corintis' $25M round (Swiss microfluidic direct-to-chip cooling claiming up to 3x lower chip temperatures than standard cold plates).
highlights: Generation stake hedges grid-timing risk on the >5 GW extended power pipeline
Corintis is an option on next-generation rack densities

productsAndServices.roadmap: Base Electron generation timeline undisclosed; Corintis tech not yet deployed at campus scale.

recentDevelopments.headline: Fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ended Aug 31): revenue $341.9M (+322%), of which HPC Hosting $262.6M ($183.5M tenant fit-out, $65.8M base rent); GAAP net loss to common $221.0M ($0.76/sh); adj. EBITDA $64.4M; NOI $58.8M; $3.7B cash vs $6.4B debt; leases unchanged at ~1.41 GW / ~$36B base term
recentDevelopments.read: Another quarter where fit-out pass-through revenue dominates the top line (54% of total) and the real operating signal is base rent plus NOI. Debt rose from ~$5.0B to $6.4B in one quarter; net loss widened on $51.7M of stock compensation, $77.4M of interest and $60.9M of derivative and investment fair-value losses. No new lease signed in the quarter beyond Delta Forge 2.

recentDevelopments.headline: Secures up to ~1 GW of potential power in Finland — first site outside the US; initial power from 2028, site being marketed to hyperscalers
recentDevelopments.read: A deliberately small first step abroad: management frames it as limited initial exposure with spend tied to customer demand, not a change from the US pipeline. It is a power option, not a lease — nothing is contracted.

recentDevelopments.headline: Building 2 Phase 2 (+75 MW, three 25 MW halls) ready for service at Polaris Forge 1; campus live capacity 250 MW of a 400 MW contract
recentDevelopments.read: Delivery cadence held: 100 MW (Oct 2025), 175 MW (Jul 2026), 250 MW (Oct 2026). Management expects initial Polaris Forge 2 operations to lift North Dakota live capacity to 300 MW by end of calendar 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2026: revenue $611.3M (+167%), adj. EBITDA $107.2M, net loss $249.2M; Q4 revenue $258.7M beat consensus by up to 148% (Zacks had $81.95M) on $152.4M of tenant fit-out; stock still fell on the debt load
recentDevelopments.read: The quarter that crystallized the APLD paradox: massive beats driven by lumpy fit-out revenue nobody models, against a balance sheet that went from $911M to $5B of debt in twelve months.

recentDevelopments.headline: Second building delivered at Polaris Forge 1 — Building 2 Phase 1 (+75 MW) ready for service; campus live capacity 175 MW
recentDevelopments.read: The delivery cadence keeps matching the promises — the execution reputation that unlocked three hyperscaler leases in four months.

recentDevelopments.headline: $1.59B senior secured notes priced at par (7.00% due 2031) for PF1's fourth building; coupon trajectory across three project-note issues: 9.25% (Nov 2025, at 97) → 6.75% (Mar 2026, at 98) → 7.00% (par)
recentDevelopments.read: The debt market repriced Applied Digital from high-yield speculation toward infrastructure credit in seven months — the same arc as the leases that back the notes.

recentDevelopments.headline: Delta Forge 2: 210 MW / ~$5.2B lease (fifth campus, new southern state) with the same high-IG hyperscaler — total contracted now 1.4 GW / ~$36B base (~$86B with renewals)
recentDevelopments.read: Third lease from one still-unnamed counterparty in seven weeks — that hyperscaler now IS the backlog (~69%), a concentration the market can't underwrite without knowing the name.

recentDevelopments.headline: Polaris Forge 3: 300 MW / ~$7.5B lease (up to $18.2B with renewals) pushes contracted capacity past 1 GW; MDU power agreement still subject to regulatory approval
recentDevelopments.read: The 1 GW milestone arrived with an asterisk — part of the contracted book still depends on utility regulatory clearance.

recentDevelopments.headline: ChronoScale separation completed — the GPU-cloud segment begins trading as CHRN; Applied Digital retains ~96–97%
recentDevelopments.read: The landlord thesis purified: long-duration lease cash flows on one ticker, short-cycle cloud risk on another.

recentDevelopments.headline: Delta Forge 1 (Boyce, LA): 300 MW / ~$7.5B lease — the mystery hyperscaler's first southern campus; stock +25% on the week with the $300M Goldman bridge
recentDevelopments.read: The franchise model proved portable out of North Dakota — and the spec-build risk taken at the January groundbreaking resolved in three months.

recentDevelopments.headline: NVIDIA's Q4 2025 13F reveals it exited its entire APLD stake (7.7M shares, ~$177M, held since the Sept 2024 $160M financing); shares fell ~8.4% after hours
recentDevelopments.read: The single most negative un-announced datapoint of the period — the ecosystem kingmaker took its validation capital elsewhere even as the lease book compounded.

recentDevelopments.headline: $2.35B 9.25% project notes priced (at 97) plus the second Macquarie preferred draw ($787.5M at 12.75% PIK); shares fell ~24% on the week
recentDevelopments.read: The cost of building without an investment-grade balance sheet, priced in public: the market briefly asked whether the AI data-center debt party was over.

recentDevelopments.headline: First hyperscaler tenant: ~$5B, 15-year, 200 MW lease at Polaris Forge 2 with a US investment-grade hyperscaler holding a ROFR on the campus's other 800 MW
recentDevelopments.read: The signing that ended the 18-month 'show me the lease' discount — and started the still-running guessing game about the tenant's identity.

recentDevelopments.headline: CoreWeave anchors Polaris Forge 1: ~$7B / 250 MW across two ~15-year leases (expanded to 400 MW / ~$11B on Aug 29)
recentDevelopments.read: The deal that converted APLD from a story stock into a landlord with a bankable book — CoreWeave's own leveraged credit remains the caveat (later addressed with restructured guarantees and a $50M letter of credit).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Applied Digital has executed the cleanest landlord conversion in the cohort: sell the cloud (ChronoScale), keep the bitcoin cash flow, and put every incremental dollar into 15-year take-or-pay leases. Basis: five campuses signed in 13 months, delivery milestones hit on schedule, and Q4 FY2026 NOI margin of 91% — the 'franchise model' language is corporate branding for a real, repeating playbook.

(High confidence) We assess counterparty concentration is the defining risk, in two layers. Basis: SEC filings show two customers = 100% of continuing revenue; the unnamed hyperscaler holds ~$25B (~69%) of the $36B backlog — an unverifiable credit until named — while CoreWeave (~31%) is itself a leveraged neocloud whose lease security Applied restructured with a $50M letter of credit, a tacit admission the landlord manages its anchor's credit risk.

(High confidence) We assess the capital structure is the price of speed and will define equity returns. Basis: ~$6.1B of project notes at 6.75–9.25%, the Macquarie preferred at 12.75% PIK with a 1.80x MOIC floor plus 15% of the HPC equity, shares outstanding up ~27% in a year, and a -$720M single-quarter FCF burn. The coupon compression across 2026 issues shows the market warming; the preferred remains the expensive tail that senior refinancing should eventually take out.

(Moderate confidence) We assess sell-side consensus is structurally unreliable for this name, making 'beats' and 'misses' poor signals. Basis: FY2026 revenue printed $611M against a Zacks full-year consensus that stood at $281M as late as April — tenant fit-out revenue (lumpy, pass-through-like) is the wedge; the market has learned to trade the debt line and NOI instead.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the next leg depends on power, not demand. Basis: 1.7 GW being marketed against a ~3 GW active / >5 GW extended utility-power pipeline, the Polaris Forge 3 MDU agreement still awaiting regulatory approval, the Base Electron generation stake (~10%; a power purchase agreement for a ~1,200 MW gas plant in North Dakota disclosed 2026-10-07) and a ~1 GW Finland option (initial power 2028) — the constraint the company itself hedges is grid timing. Collection gap: the hyperscaler tenant identity remains undisclosed; the Q1 release now places Delta Forge 1 in Louisiana and Delta Forge 2 in Alabama.

relationships.note: Anchor tenant at Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale, ND) — 400 MW / ~$11B across ~15-year take-or-pay leases.
relationships.context: CoreWeave anchored Polaris Forge 1 in June 2025 at ~$7B / 250 MW and expanded to 400 MW / ~$11B that August; 175 MW was live as of July 2026. The deal converted Applied Digital from a story stock into a landlord with a bankable book — with the caveat that CoreWeave's own leveraged credit led Applied to restructure guarantees with a $50M letter of credit.

relationships.note: Former strategic investor — NVIDIA exited its entire ~$177M stake in its Q4 2025 13F.
relationships.context: NVIDIA had held 7.7M shares (~$177M) since the September 2024 $160M financing round. Its Q4 2025 13F revealed a full exit; shares fell ~8.4% after hours. The dossier calls it the most negative un-announced datapoint of the period — the ecosystem kingmaker took its validation capital elsewhere even as the lease book compounded.
